That on 22.09.2020 at about 18.35 hours the deceased victims and the petitioners were travelling in Cruiser Toofan vehicle bearing registration No.KA-28/M-5984 from Jangatihal towards Hukkeri.

Contrary to this age, the respondent has not produced any documents.
In the absence of any other documents based on the oral evidence of PW2 and police records and medical documents are sufficient to hold that the deceased was aged 16 years at the time of the accident.
39) Of course as Laxmi aged 16 years was a teeneger and as deposed by P.W.2 deceased was studying in 8th standard, definitely the petitioner was not dependent on her.
On the other hand the deceased girl was the dependent on her petitioner.
So the petitioner cannot claim to be the dependent of the deceased girl.
As the deceased girl was aged 16 years as on the date of the accident and she had no earning capacity, this tribunal has to look into the precedents laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and Hon'ble Supreme Court.
In the present case, the deceased girl Laxmi was aged 16 years.
42) In the decision, of Kishan Gopal and another V/s Lala and others reported in (2014) 1 SCC 244 in the case of death of child aged 11 years, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has taken notional annual income of minor child at Rs. 30,000/- per annum and applied multiplier of 15 and awarded total compensation of Rs. 5,00,000/-.
In the present case, deceased girl was aged 16 years died who entirely depended on her mother.
On re-appreciation and re-examination of the evidence on record, we do not find any legal infirmity/illegality in the award passed by the Tribunal.
Hence, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the minor petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the disability would be 20% to the whole body.
The petitioner has produced document Ex.P.14 to show his date of birth as 8.9.207 and this accident occurred on 22.09.2020.
if the date of birth which is mentioned in Ex.P.14 is taken into consideration, it can be safely said that the petitioner was was aged 13 years on the date of accident.
But the Tribunal has assessed the disability of the petitioner to the whole body at 15%.
Considering the nature of injures and also the medical evidence, we are of the view that it is just and proper to consider the disability to be whole body at 43%.
The Tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.14,500/-
per month instead of assessing it at Rs.13,750/- per month as per the chart issued by the Karnataka The Divisional Controller vs Smt Avvakka W/O Kallappa Hudali on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87007077/
22 State Legal Services Authority.
27. Though the claimants have not preferred any appeal, it is the duty of the Court to award just and proper compensation in accordance with law and facts and also the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
